gloss: to drain oil; to let oil drip off

definitions.gloss: to drain off oil; to let excess oil drip off fried food
definitions.explanation: A cooking technique where freshly fried food is placed on a rack or paper towel to allow excess oil to drip away, resulting in crispier and less greasy food.

examples.japanese: ⟦{揚|あ}げたら→揚げる：16879_ageru⟧{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る。
⟦キッチンペーパー→キッチンペーパー：25045_kicchinpeepaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please drain the oil on paper towels.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しっかり→しっかり：01272_shikkari⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、サクサク⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{仕上|しあ}がる→仕上がる：11429_shiagaru⟧。
examples.english: If you drain the oil thoroughly from tempura, it turns out crispy.

notes:
A fundamental cooking expression composed of ⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧ (oil) + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ (object marker) + ⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to cut). In this context, ⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ means to separate or remove rather than to cut with a blade. This step is essential in Japanese deep-frying (⟦{揚|あ}げ{物|もの}→揚げ物：04975_agemono⟧) to achieve the prized crispy texture.

COMMON METHODS:
- ⟦{網|あみ}→網：22587_ami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る: drain on a wire rack
- ⟦キッチンペーパー→キッチンペーパー：25045_kicchinpeepaa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る: drain on paper towels
- ⟦{油切|あぶらき}り→油切り：08574_aburakiri⟧⟦{網|あみ}→網：22587_ami⟧: oil-draining rack
